label: Fan · CFD
text: Fan — CFD-checked axial PC-fan blades (printable STL)

label: Mixed · estimate
text: Mixed-flow — drop-in impeller (rough estimate, not full Fan CFD)

label: Volute · estimate
text: Volute — radial blower (rough estimate, ranking only)

label: Prop · fast estimate
text: Propeller — fast estimate (~1 s). Optional CFD check.

label: CROR · estimate
text: CROR — stacked rotors (fast estimate, not full CFD)

label: Cylindrical tip
text: Cut tip to a cylinder at tip radius so OD is constant.

label: (edited_stale ? '✎ Edited copy (not saved) — based on:' : 'Design (unlocks Preview / Assess / Export)')
Blades
text: How many blades. More = more airflow & pressure, but louder and less efficient.

label: Chord root
text: Blade WIDTH at the hub — leading edge to trailing edge (planform). Not wall thickness.

label: Chord mid
text: Blade WIDTH at mid-span (LE→TE). Not the thin wall through the blade.

label: Chord tip
text: Blade WIDTH at the tip (LE→TE). Raise this when the tip flattens (lower stagger) so the planform still covers the reference. Slider goes to 70 mm.

label: Stagger root
text: Blade PITCH angle at the hub. Higher = more axial (flow); lower = blades overlap (pressure).

label: Stagger mid
text: Blade PITCH angle at mid-span.

label: Stagger tip
text: Blade PITCH angle at the tip.

label: Section family
text: NACA = cambered airfoil with sharp LE/TE. Rounded plate = constant wall, tunable LE/TE roundness + camber (bows the blade face — the slight tip→hub curve). Wrap/lean still set the spanwise vortex planform.

label: Camber root
text: Blade SCOOP at the hub — the face curves from leading edge to trailing edge (technical name: camber). Tip-on, a scooped blade looks U-shaped; zero camber is a flat paddle. This is what matches the white reference scoop. Wrap/sickle only move the planform outline.

label: Camber mid
text: Blade SCOOP at mid-span (camber). Raise this with tip camber until the tip-on overlay matches the reference. Works on NACA and Rounded plate.

label: Camber tip
text: Blade SCOOP at the tip (camber) — usually the biggest visual match to the reference tip-on U-curve. Stock tip is ~0.12; slider goes to 0.15. Press Preview after changing.

label: Camber position
text: Where max camber sits along the chord (0.2 = near LE, 0.6 = aft). Fraction of chord — not mm.

label: Thickness span
text: Uniform wall = same mm through the blade at every station. Tapered = independent t/c. Does not set LE→TE width — that is Chord.

label: Wall thickness
text: Wall thickness through the blade (mm), held constant root→tip. This is the thin dimension — not chord/width. Typical printed fan ~1.8–2.8 mm. Use Rounded plate; set LE/TE roundness ~0.2 (full LE bullnose fights uniform wall).

label: Wall t/c root
text: Wall t/c at the hub (fraction of chord). Tapered mode only. Through-blade thickness, not LE→TE width.

label: Wall t/c mid
text: Wall t/c at mid-span. Tapered mode only.

label: Wall t/c tip
text: Wall t/c at the tip. Tapered mode only.

label: LE thick / roundness
text: LEADING-EDGE control. NACA: thickness scale (1 = stock; >1 fattens the nose). Plate: LE roundness 0–1 (1 = full bullnose bead — fights uniform wall; ~0.2 = sharp). If left at 1 with plate, LE follows TE roundness. Click Preview after changing.

label: TE thick / roundness
text: TRAILING-EDGE control. NACA: thickness scale (1 = stock; <1 thins aft; >1 fattens). Plate: TE roundness 0–1 (1 = full bullnose, ~0.2 = sharp printable TE).

label: Smooth span curves
text: Smooth span curves (PCHIP) — interpolate hub→mid→tip with a shape-preserving cubic so mid wrap/sweep/skew don't put a sharp kink in the blade. Off = linear (historical).

label: Wrap mid
text: Circumferential WRAP at mid-span — wraps blades so they overlap like a real fan.

label: Wrap tip
text: Circumferential WRAP at the tip (0 = a flat radial paddle).

label: Sweep mid
text: Axial rake of the WHOLE mid section (mm, + toward outlet / +Z). Wider range for matching reference STLs.

label: Sweep tip
text: Axial rake of the WHOLE tip section (mm, + toward outlet / +Z).

label: LE curve mid
text: Rakes only the LEADING edge at mid-span (mm) — curves the LE line, trailing edge unchanged.

label: LE curve tip
text: Rakes only the LEADING edge at the tip (mm).

label: Sickle mid
text: Sickle / LE skew at mid-span (mm) — shifts only the leading-edge region sideways in the rotation plane (scimitar). Trailing edge stays put. 0 = radial LE. Not live: press Preview. If Preview times out, the old mesh stays on screen so sickle looks like it did nothing.

label: Sickle tip
text: Sickle / LE skew at the tip (mm). Typical printed PC-fan tips sit around 4–12 mm. Same axis as Optimize → Sickle leading edge. Press Preview — a timed-out build keeps the previous orange mesh.

label: Skew mid
text: Skew (mm) — shifts the whole mid section sideways (tangentially). Fine balance/overlap tweak.

label: Skew tip
text: Skew (mm) — shifts the whole tip section sideways (tangentially). Wide range for matching reference planforms.

label: Cylindrical tip (match cover)
text: Cuts each blade tip to a cylinder at Tip radius so the outer tip face matches the fan-cover circle (constant OD). Off = legacy tips with LE/TE corners that bulge past Tip radius. Tip Round still petals the planform before the cut.

label: Tip round
text: Rounds the blade TIP — tapers the chord over the outer span so the leading & trailing edges curve together, instead of a blunt straight tip edge. 0 = square.

label: Tip round start
text: Where the tip rounding begins (fraction of span). Lower = a longer, gentler rounded tip; higher = a small rounded cap near the very tip.

label: Tip TE notches (3 boxy bites)
text: Three boxy / skewed-rectangle bites cut into the outer trailing edge (close-ref A12x25 tip TE steps). Not spanwise owl serrations and not LE tubercles. Slows Preview — wait for it to finish after changing Sickle/Wrap.

label: Tip notch depth
text: How deep each tip TE notch cuts toward mid-chord (mm). Stock ≈ 1.5 mm. Deeper = more staircase on the TE.

label: Winglet start
text: Where the WINGLET starts (fraction of span). Below this the blade is straight; beyond it the tip curls.

label: Winglet sweep
text: Winglet AXIAL bend (mm) — curls the tip forward/up out of the rotation plane (a real winglet). 0 = off.

label: Winglet lean
text: Winglet CIRCUMFERENTIAL curl (deg) — wraps the tip around the axis. 0 = off.

label: Shroud thickness
text: Radial wall of a ring fused at the blade tips (mm). 0 = open tip. Grows the outer diameter by twice this amount.

label: Shroud height
text: How much of the tip chord the ring covers. 1 = full span. Below 1 the hoop starts at the trailing edge. BEM still treats a partial ring as an open tip.

label: Hub radius
text: Hub size (mm). Smaller hub = bigger flow annulus (more airflow/efficiency); must fit the model's hub limits.

label: Tip radius / length
text: Blade LENGTH / outer radius (mm). Shrink it to make an oversized blade fit the frame (tip diameter) or trim depth.

label: Hub height (0=auto)
text: Hub HEIGHT (mm). 0 = auto (just covers the blade roots — shortest). Raise it for a taller hub; it can't go below root coverage. Needs slack above the root span before Blade on hub can shift.

label: Blade on hub
text: Where the blade roots sit on the hub (mm). 0 = centered. Positive = blades higher toward the intake (+Z), with more hub below — matches the real A12x25 which sits toward the top face. Negative = blades lower / toward the outlet. Clamped so roots stay inside the hub.

label: Hub nose (cone/dome)
text: Nose height (mm) for the cone/dome hub profile. Adds a spinner on the intake side (increases depth — may go over-spec).

label: Uneven spacing
text: Uneven-but-balanced blade spacing to spread the blade-pass tone. 0 = evenly spaced.

label: Tubercle amp
text: Tubercle amplitude — bumpy leading edge (whale-fin), delays stall.

label: Tubercle waves
text: Number of tubercle bumps along the span.

label: Serration amp
text: Serration depth — sawtooth trailing edge (owl-wing), cuts edge noise.

label: Serration teeth
text: Number of serration teeth.

label: Dimple depth
text: Dimple depth — golf-ball-style surface texture.

label: Dimple rows
text: Dimples along the chord.

label: Dimple cols
text: Dimples along the span.

label: Third CFD at operating point (~50% longer)
text: Runs a third CFD at the real hose operating pressure instead of estimating load CFM from two points. Used by Assess and by Optimize. When to use: more honest load CFM. Cost: ~50% longer per design. Risk: still RANS, not a lab measurement.

label: FDM wall roughness (ks≈0.1 mm)
text: Models FDM print roughness (~0.1 mm sand grain) on impeller + frame/stator; casing stays smooth. Used by Assess and Optimize. When to use: printed-part honesty. Cost: same solve time. Risk: slightly lower predicted CFM vs smooth walls.

label: Trials
text: How many CFD designs to try. Each trial is a full mesh+solve (often tens of minutes). Start small (8). More trials ≈ better Pareto coverage, linear wall-clock cost.

label: Continue the last Optimize run
text: Add new trials to the most recent runs/cockpit_opt_* run instead of starting a new one. The optimizer only learns from trials in the same run, so separate small runs each restart with random warm-up designs; continuing lets the trials add up. Risk: mixes settings if you changed hose/flags since the last batch. With no earlier Optimize run it continues the opened run.

label: Tip ring / shroud
text: Also search designs with a plastic tip ring fused at the blade tips (kills tip leak). When to use: ducted / sealed-tip ideas. Cost: same CFD budget, slightly different geometry stamp. Risk: ring grows OD — tip radius is capped so it still fits the frame.

label: Stator vanes
text: Replace the usual four-bar exit frame with a row of fixed guide vanes (straightens swirl). When to use: chasing pressure / efficiency after the rotor. Cost: same CFD count. Risk: can cut free CFM; mutually exclusive with stator+frame stack.

label: Stator + frame stack
text: Guide vanes first, then the four-bar frame a few mm downstream. When to use: mountable hardware that still needs OGVs. Cost: same CFD count. Risk: more blockage than stator alone; turns off plain stator.

label: Sickle leading edge
text: Forward-sweeps the leading edge in the rotation plane (scimitar / sickle shape). When to use: exploring tip loading / tone ideas. Cost: same CFD count. Risk: another geometry family — compare fairly against un-sickled runs.

label: Stepped inlet casing
text: Adds a concentric step on the circular inlet casing (not on the blade). When to use: inlet-conditioning experiments. Cost: same CFD count. Risk: casing-only change.

label: Notched tip trailing edge
text: Cuts three small bites into the trailing edge near the tip. When to use: tip-tone experiments. Cost: same CFD count. Risk: fixed recipe (not a free search variable); do not expect proven dB cuts.

label: BEM ranking screen — skip CFD below ~32 CFM
text: RANKING-ONLY blade-element screen: skip CFD if predicted hose CFM is below ~32. Not absolute CFM — ignores thickness/lean/wrap/LE-TE/plate; typically under-ranks CFD (~0.6×). When to use: large campaigns to burn fewer CFD hours. Never quote BEM beside CFD as equal.

label: Catalog GP skip below ~40 CFM free
text: Catalog Gaussian-process guess of free-delivery CFM: skip CFD when mean+uncertainty is below ~40 CFM. When to use: with a populated catalog. Cost: faster after a few scored points. Risk: weak early on; uncertain predictions still run CFD.

label: Boost + GP mean
text: With Catalog GP skip on: use a boosted-tree mean + GP uncertainty. When to use: richer catalog. Cost: tiny CPU overhead. Risk: needs scikit-learn or falls back to GP-only.

label: NN + GP mean
text: With Catalog GP skip on: use a small neural net for the CFM mean + GP uncertainty (wins over Boost if both on). When to use: experimental surrogate. Cost: tiny. Risk: needs PyTorch or falls back to GP-only.

label: Surrogate-guided (DoE→NSGA on GP→verify top-k)
text: Pro loop: space-filling DoE → fit GP/boost/NN → NSGA-II on the surrogate → verify top-k (stub by default; CFD when Docker verify is on) → refit. Uses ensemble/GP spread as the acquisition signal. When to use: explore many designs cheaply before spending CFD. Cost: CPU for DoE+NSGA; CFD only on top-k if verify is enabled. Risk: surrogate can mis-rank early; verify is the honesty gate.

label: Search RPM in PWM band
text: Treat RPM as a searchable dial inside the fan’s PWM band (not fixed nameplate speed). When to use: PWM / thermal fans. Cost: wider search → more trials to cover well. Risk: compares apples-to-oranges vs fixed-RPM campaigns.

label: PWM RPM min
text: Lowest RPM Optuna may pick when Search RPM is on (PWM band floor).

label: PWM RPM max
text: Highest RPM Optuna may pick when Search RPM is on (PWM band ceiling).
